papers.title: Trapped fermions frustrate multiterminal Josephson networks
papers.abstract: Coherent control of fermions has become a standard approach for engineering quantum devices. Here, we explore parity-induced frustration in multiterminal Josephson arrays. We focus on odd-parity Josephson trijunctions, where the presence of a trapped fermion induces a phase winding in each trijunction. Connecting these trijunctions constrains their shared phases, resulting in a long-distance phase coherence where the frustrated configurations dominate the low-energy physics. In the classical regime, these arrays map onto the Kagome XY antiferromagnet, whose established Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition yields algebraically decaying $6e$ phase correlations. We show that the $6e$ phase coherence is manifested as a pronounced third harmonic in the current-phase relation of these arrays. While quantum phase fluctuations suppress the $6e$ coherence, we show that through spin-orbit coupling they also lead to spin correlations and entanglement between the trapped fermions. Our results establish fermion-induced frustration as a route to composite superconducting coherence and phase-mediated spin entanglement in superconductor-semiconductor artificial quantum materials.

papers.title: Reconciling Models for Infinite-Layer Nickelate Superconductors: Role of Interstitial-$s$ Band or $A$-Pocket
papers.abstract: Understanding the minimal model that captures the essential physics of infinite-layer nickelate superconductors remains a central challenge. Using first-principles density-functional theory combined with dynamical mean-field theory (DFT+DMFT), we compute and compare the strongly correlated electronic structures and optical spectra of various effective models for the infinite-layer nickelate LaNiO$_2$, ranging from a $d_{x^2-y^2}$ 1-band model to a full 6-band model with all Ni-$3d$ plus an interstitial-$s$ orbital. The results demonstrate that Ni-$3d$ 5-band models overestimate the Hundness picture, whereas 6-band models, which explicitly include the interstitial-$s$ band and have an $A$-pocket, recover the characteristic Mottness physics. Importantly, the influence of the interstitial-$s$ band on the correlations of the $d_{x^2-y^2}$ band is negligible. Thus, superconductivity in infinite-layer nickelates can be reliably described within a single-band Hubbard framework, while the accurate description of inter-orbital properties such as (optical) conductivities requires the inclusion of at least the interstitial-$s$ band.

papers.title: Temperature and spatial variation of topological defects density during the crystallization of vortex nanocrystals
papers.abstract: Understanding the role of confinement while crystallizing nanocrystals is very relevant for predicting their structure and physical properties. With this aim we perform Langevin dynamics simulations of nanocrystals of the model system of few hundred vortices nucleated in micron-sized superconductors. We study the crystallization dynamics and the low-temperature structural properties of vortex nanocrystals nucleated in field-cooling conditions when changing vortex density or elasticity of the system and physical size of the samples. The low-temperature snapshots obtained in simulations present a healing effect at the edges that is in quantitative agreement with experimental data in Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+{\delta} micron-sized samples. We show that the low-temperature radial distribution of topological defects is a stationary profile frozen at a temperature below the melting line tuned by intrinsic properties of the vortex structure and on the confinement effect. These findings on the dynamics and spatial profile of topological defects can be applied to describe the physical properties of confined soft condensed matter nanocrystals in general.

papers.title: Quasi-long-range order in the quantum XY model on Sierpi\'nski gaskets
papers.abstract: Fractal geometry has recently been shown to enhance the amplitude of the superconducting order parameter, but the fate of the superconducting phase on such lattices is far less clear. Classical XY models on finitely ramified fractals have no finite-temperature transition, as the energy of a vortex stays bounded as the system grows. However, that statement concerns an infinite gasket and thermal vortices, while real fractal structures are finite by construction. It also leaves open what happens at $T = 0$, where the phase competes not with temperature but with its own quantum fluctuations. In this work we address whether superconducting phase coherence survives at $T=0$. To that end, we study the spin-$1/2$ XY ferromagnet, the phase sector of a Josephson network with at most one Cooper pair per island, thus capturing the maximum effect of quantum phase fluctuations, on both triangular and honeycomb Sierpi\'nski gaskets. By using vision-transformer neural quantum states optimized by variational Monte Carlo, we reach generations up to $G = 5$, that is $366$ sites for the triangular gasket and $609$ for the honeycomb one, well beyond the reach of exact diagonalization. We find that the transverse two-point correlator decays algebraically, $C_{xy}(r) \sim r^{-\eta}$ with $\eta \simeq 0.12\!-\!0.32$, independent of distance measured along the graph, along the fractal boundary, or in the embedding plane. Quantum phase fluctuations thus leave quasi-long-range order intact in the ground state. We further discuss the implication of these results for the superconducting response of a finite gasket at low but nonzero temperature.

papers.title: Layer-dependent $s^{\pm}$ superconducting pairing and influence of incipient bands in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ thin films on real LaSrAlO$_4$ substrate
papers.abstract: Motivated by recent advances in ambient-pressure superconducting La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ (LNO) thin films, we theoretically investigate these films by explicitly incorporating the realistic LaSrAlO$_4$ (LSAO) substrate. The Fermi-surface topology of the nickelate thin film closely resembles that of the high-pressure bulk phase, with similar $\alpha$ and $\beta$ sheets and a small hole-like $\gamma$ pocket originating from the surface bilayer (BL3). The bonding $d_{3z^2-r^2}$ state of the interfacial bilayer (BL1, adjacent to the LSAO substrate) lies only $\sim 5$ meV below the Fermi level, giving rise to an incipient $\gamma$ band, while for the middle bilayer (BL2) its energy is much lower ($\sim 95$ meV). Remarkably, no significant spontaneous charge transfer from the LSAO substrate to the LNO film is found. Instead, {\it symmetry-allowed charge disproportionation} occurs between the BLs, with hole doping in BL3 and electron doping in BL1 and BL2. Via the weak-coupling Random Phase Approximation, we find a strong $s^{\pm}$-wave superconducting pairing instability in BL3, while $d_{x^2-y^2}$ and $s^{\pm}$ are nearly degenerate in the other bilayers BL1 and BL2. Including the incipient $\gamma$ band via the Dynamical Cluster Approximation beyond weak coupling, robust $s^{\pm}$-wave pairing is observed in all three layers

papers.title: Signatures of Gaussian superconducting fluctuations in nonlocal noise magnetometry
papers.abstract: We calculate the two-point magnetic noise spectrum arising from Gaussian superconducting fluctuations, a quantity directly measurable by spin qubit pairs such as nitrogen vacancy centers in diamond. The analysis utilizes the time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau theory, reflecting the direct contribution of fluctuating Cooper pairs to the current correlations and consequent magnetic noise. We focus on two-dimensional systems and consider them both in equilibrium and under a uniform electric field. The signal is expected to be particularly pronounced in high-temperature superconductors, and we contrast our findings with the predicted signatures of a vortex liquid to offer an additional route to elucidate the nature of fluctuations in these systems. For completeness and comparison, we also present analogous results for one-dimensional wires.

papers.title: Atomic-scale Imaging of Time Reversal Breaking Supercurrents in $\mathrm{Bi_2Sr_2CaCu_2O_8}$
papers.abstract: A persistent mystery of $\mathrm{CuO_2}$-based high temperature superconductivity has been the mechanism and consequences of time reversal ($\mathcal{T}$)-symmetry breaking. Although theoretical hypotheses focus upon persistent electronic currents as a potential cause, these have been invisible to direct experimental probes. That impasse has recently been removed by development of techniques for atomic-scale supercurrent visualization. Here, by imaging the energy-resolved density of electronic states $N(r,E)$ in $\mathrm{Bi_2Sr_2CaCu_2O_8}$, we search for the specific signatures of flowing supercurrents in a disordered $d$-wave superconductor. Employing the strategy of artificial neural networks (ANN) for complex quantum matter visualization, we designed a dual-ANN (VMAP) to efficiently implement $d$-wave supercurrent visualization, achieving imaging of supercurrent speeds $V(r)$ at magnetic fields $|B| \leq$ 50 $\mu$T in $\mathrm{Bi_2Sr_2CaCu_2O_8}$. Correspondence between specific characteristics of $N(r,E)$ around each supercurrent loop and a quantum "Rosetta Stone" which translates $N(r,E)$ to $V(r)$, emphasizes the validity of $V(r)$ detection and visualization. Then, for hole-densities 0.17 $\leq p \leq$ 0.22 we observe statistically repeatable networks of supercurrent flows. Crucially, these supercurrents satisfy Kirchhoff's law at junctions within each network. Further, theoretical predictions for supercurrent speeds $V$ in disordered $d$-wave superconductors are consistent with measured 1250 m/s $< V <$ 4000 m/s, and with reported magnetic field amplitudes $|B| \approx$ 0.1 mT. Thus, detection and visualization of these supercurrent loop networks provides unique perspectives on $\mathcal{T}$-symmetry breaking in cuprates. It also emphasizes the accelerating utility of ANN techniques for physics discovery from high data volume quantum matter research.
